transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: ~75 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood CSM), Elena (BlueLattice ML Ops), Markus (Platform), Priya (SRE), Tom (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Purpose: align on incident playbook gaps after last week
- Agree on chaos-sim test runway and instrumentation checklist
- Prioritize 3 quick mitigations: stronger cache validation, short-circuit fallback, and circuit breaker on token storms
- Ownership and dates assigned

Topics: playbook orthogonalization, chaos simulation design, KV cache behavior, fallout from fallback routing, observability additions, security/audit exports, timeline for pilot

Action items (captured during call): see action_items metadata (repeated in body)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok, good afternoon everyone, uh, thanks for joining. I know this is a heavy one. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Elena: Elena here, hi.
[00:14] Markus: Markus.
[00:16] Priya: Priya on SRE.
[00:18] Tom: Tom here.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. From Redwood we have Maya and Ravi, short intros then we'll jump in.
[00:27] Maya: hey all, Maya — backend infra SE on the inference side.
[00:30] Ravi: Ravi, CSM. We'll keep notes and followups.
[00:34] Jordan: high level: after last week's outage — which folks saw as long tail latency + failed fallbacks — we promised a concrete playbook rewrite and a chaos sim to validate. Today we want to nail owners, what to test, and the quick mitigations.
[01:02] Elena: yep thanks. the customer impact was pretty clear — some revenue routes had degraded throughput for about 42 minutes and fallbacks didn't kick in cleanly, that was the scary part.
[01:12] Markus: to add: the root cause trace we saw pointed at a KV cache invalidation that caused token replays, suddenly huge KV misses and then downstream model queueing.
[01:25] Maya: yeah, the transcript of the traces show a cascade: invalidation -> bad cache warmup -> bursty cold starts -> token-timing pileup. We call that the token-storm in our notes. I think our first goal is to make the playbook orthogonal — meaning each mitigation should handle a single failure mode without overlapping ambiguous steps.
[01:48] Priya: orthogonalization sounds good; we don't want steps that contradict each other during an incident.
[01:54] Tom: can you remind us where the cache lives? in customer VPC or in Redwood Dedicated side? there was some confusion last time.
[02:03] Maya: short answer: cache layer is in the customer's VPC — it's a combination of BlueLattice-managed redis and our local KV-cache inside the Redwood runtime when deployed private. In the incident the primary invalidation originated from BlueLattice-side TTL misconfiguration, but the runtime handled the warmup poorly.
[02:26] Elena: yeah that detail is important — our infra team changed a TTL rule during a deploy window. didn't think it would ripple.
[02:33] Markus: and to be clear, the fallback routing attempted to send requests to a smaller model variant, but because the model selection relied on cached prefix heuristics, the fallback itself inherited bad state. So it's not just a hardware cold-start, it's state propagation.
[02:51] Jordan: that's the key: state propagation across fallback boundaries. So our playbook must include explicit cache-sanitization steps before fallback routing.
[02:59] [background noise, faint]
[03:02] Maya: propose three quick mitigations we can ship as hotfixes: 1) explicit KV cache validation and safe-evict flag in SDK; 2) short-circuit fallback that returns a graceful degraded response rather than attempting to rehydrate bad state; 3) rate-limiter/circuit-breaker on token-per-session to prevent token storms.
[03:20] Elena: those map to our needs. which of these require BlueLattice infra changes vs Redwood patching?
[03:26] Maya: 1) SDK flag is Redwood change (Maya's team); 2) short-circuit fallback is runtime config + playbook step (Redwood + ops); 3) circuit-breaker is a joint config — Redwood can ship a default, BlueLattice needs to tune thresholds.
[03:42] Priya: for the circuit-breaker, we prefer it to be tenant-scoped and plumbed into our telemetry so we can see when it's triggered. don't want global breakers.
[03:51] Maya: agreed. tenant-scoped hooks will be part of the patch.
[03:55] [05-second pause]
[03:58] Ravi: quick process question — for audit purposes, can Redwood push the decision timeline and all log exports to our security channel? Priya needs the chain of custody.
[04:08] Ravi: we'll attach a runbook link in the followup.
[04:11] Priya: yes please. we need SAML traces and KMS key rotation notes.
[04:15] Jordan: noted. We'll also include a minimal security export checklist.
[04:19] Tom: on chaos sim: we're thinking a 48-hour window in staging that simulates random TTL flips, redis evictions, and circuit-breaker tripping. any gotchas?
[04:31] Maya: a few: 1) ensure you have deterministic tenant traffic to reproduce stateful warmup patterns; 2) syncronize timestamps across telemetry when you fuzz TTLs; 3) ensure the prefix/KV cache warmup metric is captured.
[04:45] Markus: how intrusive is the SDK safe-evict flag? will it result in increased token usage during warmup?
[04:52] Maya: yes there is a warmup cost — but the flag can be toggled per route during the sim so we can measure delta. that's why we want a dedicated capacity slice for the tests to avoid billing/latency impacts on prod.
[05:04] Elena: can Redwood provision a short-lived dedicated test slice? our cloud ops can't spare GPUs for staging otherwise.
[05:12] Jordan: yes we can — Redwood Dedicated can provision a burst test pool for 48 hours, billed as a pilot. We'll scope it and give an estimate.
[05:21] Priya: we need the instrumentation list now — what metrics and logs to capture.
[05:25] Maya: list I'm proposing: KV cache hit/miss, prefix warmup time, model queue depth, per-tenant token-rate, fallback-routes invoked, fallback success vs degrade, request latencies p50/p90/p99, and traces showing cache invalidations with request ids.
[05:43] Markus: can you also expose internal runtime events? last time we only got partial traces, some events got redacted.
[05:49] Maya: runtime events are available via our tracing hooks; we'll create a filtered export for security redaction.
[05:55] Elena: on the playbook rewrite — please make each step idempotent and orderable, so during an incident the oncall can run steps safely even if previous steps partially ran.
[06:06] Jordan: good call. we'll add 'idempotent' tags and preconditions in the playbook.
[06:11] [sound of keyboard]
[06:14] Ravi: checklist for the chaos sim: scheduling window, test tenants list, dedicated capacity request, instrumentation dashboard links, and rollback criteria. we'll circulate a table in the followup.
[06:26] Tom: rollback criteria — what do we want? e.g., p99 latency > 3s for 5 minutes, or failed fallback rate > 10% over a 10-minute window?
[06:37] Maya: recommend both: p99 > 3s for 5 minutes OR fallback success < 90% for 10m. and a third: unexpected KV invalidation rate > X (we'll define X).
[06:49] Priya: define X as baseline + 3 sigma from historical — we'll calculate.
[06:53] Jordan: ok, we'll include that math in the runbook appendix.
[06:57] [07:00] Jordan: I want to surface the longer-term reliability improvements too: stronger model-variant isolation so state doesn't leak, smarter cache priming heuristics, and expanded fallbacks that don't rely on prefix state.
[07:14] Elena: long-term work is fine but we need immediate confidence window. 48-hour sim should give us that if we instrument correctly.
[07:22] Markus: question on security: during the sim will Redwood need access to BlueLattice's KMS? we want to keep key control on our side.
[07:31] Maya: no key handover required; logs and telemetry exports are enough. for certain cryptographic flows Redwood will run simulators without decrypting payloads. we only need meta events.
[07:41] [small crosstalk]
[07:44] Elena: earlier you mentioned 'short-circuit fallback that returns a graceful degraded response' — what's the UX impact? our product team worries about visible degraded responses.
[07:55] Jordan: good point — plan is to return a clear fallback response explaining degraded content (e.g., cached summary or a truncated response) rather than attempting a full generation that might hang. it's better UX than timeouts.
[08:11] Tom: can we have a feature-flagged behavior? default to short-circuit during sim, but enable conservative fallback in prod unless market-facing endpoints opt in.
[08:20] Maya: yes feature flag per-route is possible. we'll include that in the patch.
[08:25] [pause]
[08:28] Ravi: log housekeeping — Priya asked for chain-of-custody, we'll provide a checklist with timestamps and hashes for exported logs.
[08:36] Priya: and please include SSO/SAML session IDs with redaction rules.
[08:41] Jordan: on deliverables: Maya will prototype the SDK change; Priya will book the chaos window; Ravi will send playbook template and audit export steps; Tom will confirm success criteria.
[08:52] Elena: can we get a pilot date for production roll forward? if the sim passes, we want to pilot in prod the following week.
[08:59] Maya: conservative approach: sim on 11/18, internal review 11/20, small production pilot 11/24. if that's acceptable to BlueLattice.
[09:09] Tom: sounds reasonable.
[09:12] Jordan: let's capture next steps — (reads) run sim 11/18, deliver playbook 11/20, pilot 11/24, dedicated test capacity 11/17. This will be in the followup email.
[09:28] [short silence]
[09:32] Maya: one technical detail — the faulty behavior last time amplified because our routing fallback used model-selection heuristics that check prefix similarity; if prefix is corrupted the fallback wrongly chooses incompatible quantized variants. We'll add a compatibility check in the runtime to prevent that.
[09:52] Markus: yes that compatibility check is critical. can you put that as a precondition in the playbook? like 'do not route to variant unless compatibility flag true'.
[09:59] Maya: will do.
[10:02] Elena: any blockers on Redwood's side for delivering the patch?
[10:06] Maya: main blocker is prioritization — I need signoff to carve time this week for the SDK + runtime patch; that's why we asked for this sync and for Jordan to coordinate.
[10:16] Jordan: I'll coordinate and escalate. Ravi will also coordinate sales/legal side for the dedicated pilot.
[10:22] Ravi: yes I'll open a ticket in your CRM and attach the pilot agreement.
[10:26] [marker: 10-minute mark — conversation continued with granular steps; recaps later in call]
[40:05] [jump ahead — meeting recap segment] Jordan: ok quick recap for the 2/3 of attendees who jumped in late: we agreed on three hotfixes, a 48h chaos sim (11/18), instrumentation list, and owners. action items recorded.
[40:25] Elena: appreciate clear owners. please include rollback triggers we discussed.
[40:30] Maya: will include the math for 'X' invalidation threshold.
[40:34] Tom: security is good with the log export approach.
[40:37] Priya: one more ask — can Redwood provide a run of the sim internally and capture lessons before we do joint run? i.e., a dry run.
[40:46] Jordan: yes, Redwood will run a dry sim on 11/16 internal first.
[40:50] Elena: is that the date you proposed, 11/16?
[40:52] Jordan: yes dry run 11/16, joint run 11/18.
[40:56] [closing bits, scheduling, and next-steps confirmation]
[41:05] Ravi: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and a link to the draft playbook template.
[41:10] Maya: and I'll push an initial PR for the SDK flag into a branch and link it.
[41:14] Jordan: great. any other questions?
[41:17] Tom: none here.
[41:18] Elena: thanks everyone.
[41:20] Jordan: thanks. end call.

Meeting end: ~16:45 UTC
